strategic_capability_mapping.relationship: Closes the live-call recovery race by making recovery distinguish a currently owned MCP tools/call from an abandoned executing approval before mutating durable ledger state.

Keeps approval execution ownership inside Runtime by holding the approval claim lock from executing evidence through tools/call result terminalization and by revalidating latest state before terminal append.
Prevents live recovery, stale terminal transitions, and concurrent recovery probes from producing outcome_unknown-to-consumed chains or duplicate terminal MCP approval evidence.

answers.strategic_capabilities: Advances headless_autonomous_development, runtime_permission_enforcement, and controlled_workspace_tools by closing the MCP execution/recovery race left after RRP-3 real process-loss coverage.
answers.new_capability: Runtime now treats a live MCP tools/call owner as authoritative for that execution window: recovery_probe skips the approval when it cannot acquire the same execution-scoped lock, and only abandoned latest executing evidence can converge to outcome_unknown.
answers.why_existing_functionality_is_insufficie: RRP-3 proved real process kill/restart and stale-lock convergence, but its claim lock was released before tools/call finished and recovery did not share or re-read under that execution ownership, allowing live recovery to append outcome_unknown before the live call appended consumed.
answers.product_gap_if_skipped: A bounded headless controller could recover during an active MCP tools/call and create terminal evidence that races the successful live call, leaving misleading outcome_unknown-to-consumed history and weakening at-most-once recovery guarantees.
answers.non_duplicative: This is a corrective race-safety phase for the RRP-3 recovery boundary; it is not another approval API, schema migration, protocol canonization, or module-decomposition phase.
answers.no_new_rpc: Yes. RRP-3.1 uses existing mcp.tool.approve, tool.execute, task.start, and headless.run.recovery_probe Runtime boundaries.
answers.no_new_summary: Yes. The phase adds bounded behavior evidence to the existing ledger flow, E2E harness, release audit, and phase manifest only.
answers.runtime_behavior_change: MCP approval execution now holds the approval claim lock across executing append, tools/call, result normalization, and terminal append; recovery uses a nonblocking same-lock attempt, re-reads latest approval state under the lock, skips live owners, and appends at most one outcome_unknown only for latest executing evidence.
answers.headless_autonomous_contribution: External headless controllers can call the existing recovery probe without risking mutation of a live Runtime-owned MCP call, while actual abandoned executing evidence still converges finitely and fail-closed.
answers.milestone_progress: Closes the RRP-3.1 MCP execution/recovery race and makes the real process-loss E2E CI-required through the existing CI-invoked VSIX check path, while Runtime Release Ready remains false until the remaining Runtime P0/P1 blockers and owner license/publish decisions are handled.

exit_criteria: MCP approval execution holds a shared execution-scoped advisory lock from executing claim through tools/call completion and terminal approval append.
Recovery uses a nonblocking attempt on the same lock and performs no ledger mutation when a live execution owner holds it.
Recovery rereads latest matching approval evidence under the lock and appends outcome_unknown only when latest state is executing with matching required binding fields.
Terminalization rereads latest matching approval evidence and refuses terminal-to-terminal or changed-fingerprint transitions.

safety_boundary: Rust Runtime remains the execution, admission, replay, ledger, permission, recovery, and tool authority.
CLI and VSIX remain thin transport/projection/validation layers.
MCP approval state and recovery evidence are narrowing-only and cannot grant authority.
non_goals: Does not claim Runtime Release Ready.
Does not start durable schema migration, full CI workflow hardening, protocol/event canonization, module decomposition, platform/deadline/durability hardening, or OSS license/publish work.
Does not add scheduler, daemon, hosted supervisor, generic shell, arbitrary process execution, package distribution, or signing infrastructure.
rejected_alternatives: Rejected using lock-file existence or deletion as authority because durable MCP approval state remains the Runtime-owned source of truth.
Rejected PID-age or timeout-only stale-lock takeover because local Runtime v0 can rely on OS-owned advisory file lock release after process loss while treating residual files as non-authoritative.
Rejected automatically retrying tools/call from outcome_unknown because external MCP side effects may already have occurred before Runtime process loss.
Rejected placing recovery responsibility in CLI, VSIX, an external supervisor, or manual operator cleanup because RRP-3.1 preserves recovery through public Runtime boundaries.
technical_debt: real-process-loss-recovery-e2e remains closed with RRP-3.1 race-safety correction.

runtime-release-guard-ci remains open for the later full release-gate hardening phase; direct .github workflow wiring for RRP-3 E2E was blocked by missing OAuth workflow scope, so this phase enforces the E2E through the existing CI-invoked VSIX check path.
Durable schema migration, protocol/event canonization, module decomposition reevaluation, platform/deadline/durability hardening, and owner license/publish decisions remain open.
next_capability_rationale: After RRP-3.1 lands, continue with the next explicit Runtime-owned release-readiness phase rather than claiming Runtime Release Ready.

runtime_release_dod: RRP-3.1 closes the Runtime-owned MCP execution/recovery race for live tools/call ownership, latest-state terminalization, concurrent recovery, and CI-required E2E coverage through the existing VSIX check path.
Runtime Release Ready remains false until the remaining runtime P0/P1 blockers and owner license/publish decision are resolved.
runtime_boundary_contracts: Recovery continues through existing public Runtime JSON-RPC boundaries including task.start, mcp.tool.approve, tool.execute, and headless.run.recovery_probe.
CLI and VSIX remain thin transport/projection layers over Runtime-owned contracts.
external_control_plane_responsibilities: External scheduling, queueing, worker leases, hosted isolation, retry policy, metrics, alerts, SLA, tenant administration, billing, and secret-provider operations remain outside this local Runtime v0 phase.
No external controller gains authority to decide MCP approval claim, replay, completion, or recovery state.
external_adapter_responsibilities: Forge, pull request, review, notification, SIEM, OTel, language verifier, customer integration, and hosted MCP adapter responsibilities remain outside RRP-3.1.
No external adapter is required to manually delete locks or directly mutate Runtime ledger state.
commercial_solution_readiness: Packaging, distribution, signing, notarization, enterprise administration, operational runbooks, support, and commercial release decisions remain out of scope.
Cargo license and publish settings remain owner-decision items and are not changed by RRP-3.1.
